citations.quote:
Fix $r,n\ge1$ and work in the universal cyclotomic algebra $H_{r,n}$ of [[def-hh-multiplicative-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]], with parameters $Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r$, commuting Jucys–Murphy generators $L_i=X_i$, and finite generators $T_i$. For an $r$-multipartition $\lambda$, put $a_c=\sum_{d<c}|\lambda^{(d)}|$ and define
$$u_\lambda=\prod_{c=2}^{r}\ \prod_{i=1}^{a_c}(L_i-u_c).$$
Let $t^\lambda$ be the row-standard initial multitableau from [[def-hh-cell-datum-dominance-and-cell-ideals]]. Let $S_\lambda$ be the subgroup of $S_n$ that permutes labels within each row of $t^\lambda$, and set $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$ and $m_\lambda=u_\lambda x_\lambda$. The anti-involution $*$ is the generator-fixing map of [[lem-hh-cyclotomic-anti-involution-fixes-generators]].

For a standard multitableau $t$, use the right entry action $t\cdot w:=w^{-1}\cdot t$, where the left action applies $w$ to every entry. Let $d(t)$ be the unique permutation with $t^\lambda\cdot d(t)=t$. Standardness implies that $d(t)$ is the distinguished minimal representative for its row-stabilizer coset. For standard $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$, define
$$m_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}.$$
These are specified elements of $H_{r,n}$; this definition does not assert their linear independence or cellularity.

Fix $r,n\ge1$ and use the independent units $Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r$ of [[def-hh-multiplicative-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]. An **$r$-multipartition** of $n$ is a tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(r)})$ of ordinary partitions whose total number of boxes is $n$. Its boxes are triples $(c,a,b)$ with $1\le c\le r$, $a\ge1$, and $1\le b\le\lambda^{(c)}_a$. Order the boxes within component $c$ by the transitive closure of $(c,a,b)<(c,a,b+1)$ and $(c,a,b)<(c,a+1,b)$; boxes in different components are incomparable.

A **standard multitableau** $t$ of shape $\lambda$ is a bijective filling of the boxes by $1,\ldots,n$ that increases along every row and column. Equivalently, it is a linear extension of this finite box poset. Write $\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)$ for the set of such fillings and

$$ \operatorname{res}_t(i)=u_cQ^{b-a}\quad\text{if entry }i\text{ occupies }(c,a,b). $$

The **generic content field** is $K=\mathbb Q(Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r)$, the fraction field of $R$. The contents of distinct addable boxes of any multipartition are distinct in $K$. If two boxes in one component have the same content, they lie on one diagonal; the right and lower boxes immediately between them are distinct required predecessors of the southeast box. Consequently, for three consecutive labels $i,i+1,i+2$ in a standard multitableau, the first and third contents cannot agree. In particular every pair of contents among three consecutive labels is distinct in $K$. If two boxes in one component have content exponents differing by $1$, then they are comparable in the box order, so interchanging adjacent labels in a standard multitableau never gives a content ratio $Q$ or $Q^{-1}$.

Let $R_A=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1}]$ and let $H_n$ be the type-A Hecke algebra on $T_1,\ldots,T_{n-1}$ with braid relations and $(T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0$. For a partition $\lambda\vdash n$, let $t^\lambda$ be row-filled, $S_\lambda$ its row subgroup, $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and
$$m_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*x_\lambda T_{d(t)}$$
for standard $\lambda$-tableaux, with the tableau action and distinguished representatives fixed in [[def-hh-cyclotomic-murphy-elements]]. Then the $m_{st}$ form an $R_A$-basis of $H_n$, $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$, and the spans $H_n^{\trianglerighteq\lambda}$ and $H_n^{\triangleright\lambda}$ of shapes respectively dominating and strictly dominating $\lambda$ are two-sided ideals. For every $h\in H_n$ and standard $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$,
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}r_{t,v}(h)m_{sv}\pmod{H_n^{\triangleright\lambda}},$$
where $r_{t,v}(h)\in R_A$ does not depend on $s$. The proof is integral over $R_A$; it does not divide by $Q+1$ or assume semisimplicity.

Let $A=\mathbb Z[Q,Q^{-1}]$ and let $H_{n,A}$ have braid relations and $(T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0$. For a composition $\alpha$ of $n$, let $x_\alpha=\sum_{w\in S_\alpha}T_w$ and let $s,t$ be row-standard $\alpha$-tableaux. Define $m^\alpha_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*x_\alpha T_{d(t)}$ using [[def-hh-cyclotomic-murphy-elements]]. For row-standard tableaux of possibly different shapes, write $u\unrhd_{\rm tab}s$ when, for every label cutoff $m$ and row cutoff $j$, the number of entries at most $m$ in the first $j$ rows of $u$ is at least the corresponding number for $s$. In the unique standard-Murphy expansion
$$m^\alpha_{st}=\sum_{\mu\vdash n}\ \sum_{u,v\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)}c_{uv}m^\mu_{uv},$$
each nonzero coefficient satisfies $u\unrhd_{\rm tab}s$, $v\unrhd_{\rm tab}t$, and $\mu\unrhd\bar\alpha$, where $\bar\alpha$ is the partition obtained by sorting the parts of $\alpha$. These are integral identities over $A$, and they specialize to every commutative ring with a unit Hecke parameter. Generic semisimplicity is used to prove coordinate vanishing over $A$; semisimplicity is not assumed after specialization.

Let $(S,m)$ be a finite Coxeter matrix with presented group $W$, length $\ell$ and geometric representation $\sigma:W\to\mathrm{GL}_K(E)$ as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], [[def-hh-geometric-coxeter-representation-and-roots]] and [[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]], and let $J\subseteq S$.

1. **Support and reduction.** For every $w\in W$ the set $S(w)$ of letters occurring in a reduced expression of $w$ is independent of the reduced expression, and every word in $S$ representing $w$ can be transformed into a reduced expression by repeatedly deleting two letters (Tits reduction, using only letters already present). Consequently
$$W_J=\langle J\rangle=\{w\in W:S(w)\subseteq J\}.$$
2. **Intrinsic parabolic presentation.** Let $W_J^\ast$ be the group presented by the restricted Coxeter matrix $(J,m|_J)$ in the sense of [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]. The canonical homomorphism $W_J^\ast\to W_J$, $s\mapsto s$, is an isomorphism. Hence $(W_J,J)$ is a Coxeter system, its intrinsic length function $\ell_J$ agrees with the ambient length $\ell$ on $W_J$, and $W_J\cap S=J$.
3. **Minimal coset representatives.** Every right coset $W_J a:=\{ua:u\in W_J\}$ ($a\in W$, [[def-coset]]) has a unique element $d$ of minimal length; it is characterized by $\ell(sd)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$, and it satisfies
$$\ell(ud)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)\qquad\text{for all }u\in W_J .$$
Equivalently, every $w\in W$ has a unique factorization $w=u\,d$ with $u\in W_J$ and $d$ the minimal representative of the right coset $W_J d$, and then $\ell(w)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)$. By inversion ($w\mapsto w^{-1}$ preserves lengths and interchanges the two coset families $\{W_Ja\}$ and $\{aW_J\}$), every left coset $aW_J:=\{au:u\in W_J\}$ has a unique minimal element $d$, characterized by $\ell(ds)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$ and satisfying $\ell(du)=\ell(d)+\ell(u)$ for all $u\in W_J$.
4. **Type A.** Let $n\ge2$, $S=\{s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\}$ and $m(s_i,s_j):=3$ if $|i-j|=1$, $m(s_i,s_j):=2$ if $|i-j|>1$ (a Coxeter matrix of type $A_{n-1}$). Then $s_i\mapsto(i\ i+1)$ extends to an isomorphism $W\to S_n$ (the letters $1,\dots,n$ carry the library's symmetric group by the order-preserving identification with $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, under which $(i\ i+1)$ is the adjacent transposition $(i-1\ i)$), and for every $w\in W$,
$$\ell(w)=\operatorname{inv}\bigl(\varphi(w)\bigr),$$
the inversion number of the corresponding permutation ([[def-inversions-inversion-number-and-sign]]). In particular a word in the $s_i$ is reduced if and only if its length equals the inversion number of its value.

derivations.claim: Let $n_c=|\alpha^{(c)}|$ and $a_c=\sum_{d<c}n_d$. Write $S_\eta=S_{n_1}\times\cdots\times S_{n_r}$ for the subgroup permuting labels inside the consecutive component intervals. Every row-standard $s$ has a unique factorization $s=s_0\cdot w_s$ with $s_0$ of initial kind and $w_s$ the distinguished representative for the component coset; similarly $t=t_0\cdot w_t$. By [F4], $d(s)=d(s_0)w_s$, $d(t)=d(t_0)w_t$, and both lengths add. For any finite generator $T_i$ inside component interval $k$, the factors of $u_\alpha$ with index $c\le k$ use only $L_j$ with $j<i$ and commute distantly; factors with $c>k$ contain both $L_i,L_{i+1}$ symmetrically and commute by the Murphy divided-difference relation. Thus $u_\alpha$ commutes with all of $H(S_\eta)$.

For initial-kind $s_0,t_0$, the row group and distinguished tableau permutations split into their component intervals. Since $u_\alpha$ commutes with $S_\eta$, the finite part of $m^\alpha_{s_0t_0}$ is a product of ordinary type-A row Murphy elements, one for each component. Apply the ordinary type-A composition-to-partition straightening [F3] separately in each component. Every output component partition dominates the sorted input component partition. The row-tableau prefix inequalities are exactly the componentwise inequalities from [F3]. The component factors commute because their simple-generator intervals are disjoint, so multiplying their finite expansions gives the asserted initial-kind expansion and componentwise dominance.

Restore arbitrary $s,t$ by multiplying each initial-kind term on the left by $T_{w_s}^*$ and on the right by $T_{w_t}$. Length additivity makes these products the Murphy elements indexed by the relabeled row-standard tableaux, without lower-length corrections. The component assignments are preserved because the same component coset representatives act on every term. To check tableau-prefix dominance after relabeling, fix a global label cutoff $m$. Since each $w_s$ preserves order within an initial component interval, the labels of that interval sent to values at most $m$ form an initial segment. Every cumulative row count of a relabeled tableau is therefore the corresponding componentwise row-prefix count at that segment length, where the inequalities have already been proved in step 2.1. The same argument applies to $w_t$.

For each multipartition $\lambda$, the exact finite row-module action expresses every $m_{st}T_i$ as a combination of row-standard elements of shape $\lambda$ with first index $s$. Apply the componentwise expansion just proved: all output shapes dominate $\lambda$ component by component, so $N^{\unrhd\lambda}$ is a right ideal for the finite Hecke subalgebra. Applying $*$ gives left closure. The strict span is the sum of these ideals over shapes strictly dominating $\lambda$, so it is also a two-sided ideal for that subalgebra. This argument proves ideal closure before using a fixed-first-index congruence.

Now take $s=t^\lambda$. In every same-shape standard output term from that componentwise expansion the first tableau $u$ dominates $t^\lambda$. The row-filled tableau is maximal for every row-prefix count among standard tableaux of this fixed shape, so equality of all the counts forces $u=t^\lambda$. Thus $m_{t^\lambda,t}T_i$ is a linear combination of the $m_{t^\lambda,v}$ modulo $N^{\triangleright\lambda}$. Its coefficients depend only on $t,T_i$ and $\lambda$. Multiply this congruence on the left by $T_{d(s)}^*$ for arbitrary standard $s$. The error remains in $N^{\triangleright\lambda}$ by step 4.1, and the displayed terms become $m_{sv}$. This proves the asserted finite-generator law with coefficients independent of $s$.

In $H_{r,n}$ define

$$ L_1=X_1,\qquad L_i=Q^{1-i}T_{i-1}\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_{i-1}\quad(2\le i\le n). $$

Then $L_i=X_i$ for every $i$, so the $L_i$ commute and are units. For $1\le i<n$ they satisfy

$$ T_iL_iT_i=QL_{i+1},\qquad T_iL_i=L_{i+1}T_i-(Q-1)L_{i+1},\qquad T_iL_{i+1}=L_iT_i+(Q-1)L_{i+1}, $$

and $T_iL_j=L_jT_i$ when $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$. More generally, for every polynomial $f\in R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$,

$$ T_if(L_1,\ldots,L_n)=f(s_iL_1,\ldots,s_iL_n)T_i-(Q-1)L_{i+1}\frac{f(L_1,\ldots,L_n)-f(s_iL_1,\ldots,s_iL_n)}{L_i-L_{i+1}}, $$

where $s_i$ interchanges the $i$th and $(i+1)$st variables and the displayed divided difference is a polynomial. In particular the cyclotomic relation transports as

$$ T_ip(L_i)=p(L_{i+1})T_i-(Q-1)L_{i+1}\frac{p(L_i)-p(L_{i+1})}{L_i-L_{i+1}}. $$

When $p(L_i)=0$, this gives $p(L_{i+1})T_i=(Q-1)L_{i+1}(p(L_i)-p(L_{i+1}))/(L_i-L_{i+1})$; the cyclotomic quotient guarantees this only for $i=1$. It does **not** impose $p(L_i)=0$ for every $i$.

Fix integers $r,n\ge1$. Put $R=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1},u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_r^{\pm1}]$ and $p(X)=\prod_{a=1}^r(X-u_a)$. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{aff}}$ be the unital associative $R$-algebra on generators $T_1,\ldots,T_{n-1}$ and $X_1^{\pm1},\ldots,X_n^{\pm1}$, with central $R$-action, subject to

$$ (T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\ (|i-j|>1), $$

$$ X_jX_k=X_kX_j,\qquad T_iX_j=X_jT_i\ (j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad T_iX_iT_i=QX_{i+1}. $$

Here the braid relation is imposed for $1\le i<n-1$ and the distant commutation relation for $1\le i,j<n$. Define the **multiplicative cyclotomic Hecke algebra of level $r$ and rank $n$** by

$$ H_{r,n}=\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{aff}}/(p(X_1)), $$

where $(p(X_1))$ denotes the two-sided ideal it generates. The unit $Q$ and the quadratic relation make every $T_i$ invertible, with $T_i^{-1}=Q^{-1}(T_i-(Q-1))$. The cyclotomic relation also gives the polynomial inverse

$$ X_1^{-1}=(-1)^{r+1}(u_1\cdots u_r)^{-1}\bigl(X_1^{r-1}-e_1X_1^{r-2}+\cdots+(-1)^{r-1}e_{r-1}\bigr), $$

where $e_k$ is the $k$th elementary symmetric polynomial in $u_1,\ldots,u_r$. The presentation already includes inverse generators; this formula records that the quotient does not require a separate inverse parameter. For $i\ge1$, write $X_{i+1}=Q^{-1}T_iX_iT_i$ when using the recursion determined by the affine relation.

This is the multiplicative presentation. It is not the additive degenerate cyclotomic presentation obtained after setting a parameter equal to $1$ and changing generators.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $A$ be a unital associative $R$-algebra. A **cell datum** for $A$ consists of a finite poset $(\Lambda,\ge)$, finite sets $T(\lambda)$ for $\lambda\in\Lambda$, an $R$-basis $\{C^\lambda_{s,t}:\lambda\in\Lambda,\ s,t\in T(\lambda)\}$ of $A$, and an $R$-linear involutive algebra anti-automorphism $*$ satisfying $({C^\lambda_{s,t}})^*=C^\lambda_{t,s}$ and the following coefficient-independence axiom: for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$, $s,t\in T(\lambda)$, and $a\in A$, there are coefficients $r^\lambda_{t,v}(a)\in R$, independent of $s$, such that
$$C^\lambda_{s,t}a\equiv\sum_{v\in T(\lambda)}r^\lambda_{t,v}(a)C^\lambda_{s,v}\pmod{A^{>\lambda}},$$
where $A^{>\lambda}$ is the $R$-span of basis elements $C^\mu_{u,v}$ with $\mu>\lambda$. Write $A^{\ge\lambda}$ for the span with $\mu\ge\lambda$.

For multipartitions $\lambda,\mu$ of $n$ with $r$ ordered components, write $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ if for every component $1\le c\le r$ and row cutoff $j\ge0$,
$$\sum_{d<c}|\lambda^{(d)}|+\sum_{i=1}^{j}\lambda_i^{(c)} \ \ge\ \sum_{d<c}|\mu^{(d)}|+\sum_{i=1}^{j}\mu_i^{(c)},$$
with missing rows padded by zero. Write $\lambda\triangleright\mu$ when $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ and $\lambda\ne\mu$. The **row-standard initial multitableau** $t^\lambda$ fills component $1$ row by row, then component $2$ row by row, and so on, using $1,\ldots,n$ in order.

Fix $r,n\ge1$ and work in the universal cyclotomic algebra $H_{r,n}$ of [[def-hh-multiplicative-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]], with parameters $Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r$, commuting Jucys–Murphy generators $L_i=X_i$, and finite generators $T_i$. For an $r$-multipartition $\lambda$, put $a_c=\sum_{d<c}|\lambda^{(d)}|$ and define
$$u_\lambda=\prod_{c=2}^{r}\ \prod_{i=1}^{a_c}(L_i-u_c).$$
Let $t^\lambda$ be the row-standard initial multitableau from [[def-hh-cell-datum-dominance-and-cell-ideals]]. Let $S_\lambda$ be the subgroup of $S_n$ that permutes labels within each row of $t^\lambda$, and set $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$ and $m_\lambda=u_\lambda x_\lambda$. The anti-involution $*$ is the generator-fixing map of [[lem-hh-cyclotomic-anti-involution-fixes-generators]].

For a standard multitableau $t$, use the right entry action $t\cdot w:=w^{-1}\cdot t$, where the left action applies $w$ to every entry. Let $d(t)$ be the unique permutation with $t^\lambda\cdot d(t)=t$. Standardness implies that $d(t)$ is the distinguished minimal representative for its row-stabilizer coset. For standard $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$, define
$$m_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}.$$
These are specified elements of $H_{r,n}$; this definition does not assert their linear independence or cellularity.

Let $\alpha=(\alpha^{(1)},\ldots,\alpha^{(r)})$ be a multicomposition of $n$: each $\alpha^{(c)}$ is a finite sequence of nonnegative row lengths, and the total of all parts is $n$. Let $\bar\alpha^{(c)}$ be the partition obtained by sorting the parts of component $c$, and write $\bar\alpha=(\bar\alpha^{(1)},\ldots,\bar\alpha^{(r)})$. Define $u_\alpha$ by the formula for $u_\lambda$ using the component totals, let $x_\alpha$ be the sum over the row subgroup of the row-filled multicomposition tableau, and set $m^\alpha_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*u_\alpha x_\alpha T_{d(t)}$ for row-standard multitableaux $s,t$ of shape $\alpha$.

Then $m^\alpha_{st}$ is an $R$-linear combination of standard cyclotomic Murphy elements $m^\mu_{uv}$ with $\mu^{(c)}\unrhd\bar\alpha^{(c)}$ for every component $c$, and with $\operatorname{comp}_u=\operatorname{comp}_s$ and $\operatorname{comp}_v=\operatorname{comp}_t$. Define $u\unrhd_{\rm tab}s$ by requiring, for every label cutoff $m$, component $c$, and row cutoff $k$, that the number of labels at most $m$ in components $1,\ldots,c-1$ plus the first $k$ rows of component $c$ of $u$ is at least the corresponding number for $s$. Then the output tableaux also satisfy $u\unrhd_{\rm tab}s$ and $v\unrhd_{\rm tab}t$.

In particular, for a multipartition $\lambda$, standard $s,t$, and every finite generator $T_i$,
$$m_{st}T_i\equiv\sum_v r_{t,v}(T_i)m_{sv}\pmod{N^{\triangleright\lambda}},$$
with coefficients independent of $s$. Consequently $N^{\unrhd\lambda}$ and $N^{\triangleright\lambda}$ are two-sided ideals for the finite Hecke subalgebra.

Let $(S,m)$ be a finite Coxeter matrix with presented group $W$, length $\ell$ and geometric representation $\sigma:W\to\mathrm{GL}_K(E)$ as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], [[def-hh-geometric-coxeter-representation-and-roots]] and [[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]], and let $J\subseteq S$.

1. **Support and reduction.** For every $w\in W$ the set $S(w)$ of letters occurring in a reduced expression of $w$ is independent of the reduced expression, and every word in $S$ representing $w$ can be transformed into a reduced expression by repeatedly deleting two letters (Tits reduction, using only letters already present). Consequently
$$W_J=\langle J\rangle=\{w\in W:S(w)\subseteq J\}.$$
2. **Intrinsic parabolic presentation.** Let $W_J^\ast$ be the group presented by the restricted Coxeter matrix $(J,m|_J)$ in the sense of [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]. The canonical homomorphism $W_J^\ast\to W_J$, $s\mapsto s$, is an isomorphism. Hence $(W_J,J)$ is a Coxeter system, its intrinsic length function $\ell_J$ agrees with the ambient length $\ell$ on $W_J$, and $W_J\cap S=J$.
3. **Minimal coset representatives.** Every right coset $W_J a:=\{ua:u\in W_J\}$ ($a\in W$, [[def-coset]]) has a unique element $d$ of minimal length; it is characterized by $\ell(sd)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$, and it satisfies
$$\ell(ud)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)\qquad\text{for all }u\in W_J .$$
Equivalently, every $w\in W$ has a unique factorization $w=u\,d$ with $u\in W_J$ and $d$ the minimal representative of the right coset $W_J d$, and then $\ell(w)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)$. By inversion ($w\mapsto w^{-1}$ preserves lengths and interchanges the two coset families $\{W_Ja\}$ and $\{aW_J\}$), every left coset $aW_J:=\{au:u\in W_J\}$ has a unique minimal element $d$, characterized by $\ell(ds)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$ and satisfying $\ell(du)=\ell(d)+\ell(u)$ for all $u\in W_J$.
4. **Type A.** Let $n\ge2$, $S=\{s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\}$ and $m(s_i,s_j):=3$ if $|i-j|=1$, $m(s_i,s_j):=2$ if $|i-j|>1$ (a Coxeter matrix of type $A_{n-1}$). Then $s_i\mapsto(i\ i+1)$ extends to an isomorphism $W\to S_n$ (the letters $1,\dots,n$ carry the library's symmetric group by the order-preserving identification with $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, under which $(i\ i+1)$ is the adjacent transposition $(i-1\ i)$), and for every $w\in W$,
$$\ell(w)=\operatorname{inv}\bigl(\varphi(w)\bigr),$$
the inversion number of the corresponding permutation ([[def-inversions-inversion-number-and-sign]]). In particular a word in the $s_i$ is reduced if and only if its length equals the inversion number of its value.

Let $n\ge2$, $R_0=\mathbb Z[Q,Q^{-1}]$, and $A=R_0[X_1^{\pm1},\ldots,X_n^{\pm1}]$ as in [[def-hh-type-a-weight-lattice-laurent-ring-and-divided-differences]]. Let $F$ be the free associative unital $R_0$-algebra on symbols $T_1,\ldots,T_{n-1},X_1^{\pm1},\ldots,X_n^{\pm1}$ and let $I$ be the two-sided ideal generated by the following relations:

1. The $X_j$ commute and $X_jX_j^{-1}=X_j^{-1}X_j=1$.
2. $(T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0$ for $1\le i<n$.
3. The $T_i$ satisfy the type-$A_{n-1}$ braid relations: $T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1}$ for $1\le i<n-1$, and $T_iT_j=T_jT_i$ when $|i-j|>1$.
4. The Bernstein cross-relations on the Laurent generators are
$$
T_iX_j=s_i(X_j)T_i+(Q-1)D_i(X_j)\qquad(1\le i<n,\ 1\le j\le n).
$$

Define
$$
H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}:=F/I.
$$
The coefficient map $A\to H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}$ sends each Laurent monomial to the corresponding word in the $X_j$; its injectivity and the resulting $A$-module basis are the conclusion of [[thm-hh-affine-type-a-bernstein-pbw]], not an assumption in this definition. The normalization is multiplicative: $Q$ is a unit, $T_i^2=(Q-1)T_i+Q$, and $T_i$ is invertible. It matches the finite Hecke normalization of [[lem-hh-hecke-anti-involution-bar-and-normalization]] under $Q=v^2$ and $T_i=vU_i$, where $(U_i-v)(U_i+v^{-1})=0$.

derivations.claim: By the affine recursion in [F1],$T_{a_k}\cdots T_1X_1T_1\cdots T_{a_k}=Q^{a_k}L_{a_k+1},$ including $a_k=0$. By definition $u_{\mathbf b}=u_{\mathbf a}(L_{a_k+1}-u_k)$. Since the $L_j$ commute, multiplying the first identity by $u_{\mathbf a}$ and substituting $L_{a_k+1}=u_k+(L_{a_k+1}-u_k)$ proves the displayed shift identity.

For a multipartition $\lambda$, let $n_c=|\lambda^{(c)}|$, $a_c=\sum_{d<c}n_d$, and $\eta=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)$. Write $d(t)=yc$ with $y\in S_\eta$ and $c$ the distinguished component-coset representative, so $t=t^\lambda\cdot y\cdot c$. The tableau $t^\lambda\cdot y$ is standard: $c$ preserves the order of labels within each component interval, so undoing $c$ preserves every row and column inequality of $t$. Let $k$ be the component containing label $1$ in $t^\lambda\cdot c$. The factorization of $c$ is $c=s_{a_k}\cdots s_1c_0$, where $c_0$ fixes $1$ and uses only $s_i$ with $i\ge2$. Because $t^\lambda\cdot y$ is standard, $y$ fixes the first label $a_k+1$ of component $k$. The element $u_{\mathbf a}$ commutes with $T_y$, and $u_{\mathbf b}=u_{\mathbf a}(L_{a_k+1}-u_k)$ also commutes with $T_y$: $y$ fixes index $a_k+1$, and its remaining simple generators are distant from $L_{a_k+1}$. Also $T_{c_0}$ commutes with $X_1$ by [F6].

Set $C=T_1\cdots T_{a_k}$ and $D=C^{-1}=T_{a_k}^{-1}\cdots T_1^{-1}$. Multiply the identity of step 1.1 on the right by $DT_{c_0}$. The middle factors $C$ cancel with $D$, and $T_{c_0}$ commutes with $X_1$, so$u_{\mathbf a}T_cX_1=u_{\mathbf a}h_1+u_{\mathbf b}h_2$ for finite-Hecke elements $h_1,h_2$ (explicitly, $h_1=Q^{a_k}u_kDT_{c_0}$ and $h_2=Q^{a_k}DT_{c_0}$). Therefore$m_{s,t}X_1=T_{d(s)}^*x_\lambda T_y\bigl(u_{\mathbf a}h_1+u_{\mathbf b}h_2\bigr).$ The first summand is governed by [F4], since $u_{\mathbf a}x_\lambda=m_\lambda$.

If $k=1$, then $n_1\ge1$, so $a_c\ge1$ for every $c\ge2$. The vector $\mathbf b$ has $b_1=1$ and $b_c=a_c$ for $c\ge2$, hence $u_{\mathbf b}$ contains $\prod_{c=1}^r(L_1-u_c)=p(L_1)=0$ by [F2]. Thus the shifted second summand vanishes in this case.

Suppose $k>1$. Define the multicomposition $
u$ by adding a final row of size $1$ to component $k-1$, reducing the first row of component $k$ by $1$, and leaving all other rows unchanged. Its cumulative component vector is $\mathbf b$. Let $l=\lambda^{(k)}_1$, let $G_1$ permute $a_k+1,\ldots,a_k+l$, and let $G_2$ fix $a_k+1$ and permute the other entries in this interval. The length-additive coset decomposition gives$x_\lambda=\sum_{i=1}^lT_{c_i}^*x_
u,$ where $c_1,\ldots,c_l$ are the distinguished representatives of $G_2 ackslash G_1$ in increasing length. Each tableau $u_i=t^
u\cdot c_i\cdot d(s)$ is row standard: the labels $(a_k+1)d(s)<\cdots<(a_k+l)d(s)$ occur increasingly in the first row of component $k$ of $s$, and $c_i$ moves exactly one of them to the new final row of component $k-1$. Consequently $\operatorname{comp}_{u_i}(j)=\operatorname{comp}_s(j)$ except on those moved entries, where the component changes from $k$ to $k-1$. Since $u_{\mathbf b}x_
u=m_
u$, it follows that$T_{d(s)}^*x_\lambda u_{\mathbf b}=\sum_{i=1}^l m^
u_{u_i,t^
u}.$ The shifted summand in step 2.1 is this sum multiplied on the right by the finite element $T_yh_2$, so [F4] straightens it to standard terms.

The component sizes of $\nu$ move one box from component $k$ to component $k-1$. Before component $k-1$, cumulative dominance counts agree with $\lambda$; at the final row of component $k-1$ the count increases by one. At component $k$, the previous-component increase is canceled by the decrement of its first row; at later components the total sizes agree again. Sorting the rows of each component into a partition can only increase its row-prefix sums. Thus the partition shape obtained from $\nu$ strictly dominates $\lambda$, and every straightened shape in the shifted summand strictly dominates $\lambda$. For $k=1$ the shifted summand was zero by step 2.2. The unshifted summand has the fixed-first-index finite-generator law by [F4]. Hence multiplication of any standard Murphy element by $X_1$ has only shapes $\unrhd\lambda$, with same-shape first index unchanged and coefficients independent of that first index.

The cyclotomic relation has unit constant coefficient $(-1)^r\prod_cu_c$. Writing $p(X_1)=X_1^r+c_{r-1}X_1^{r-1}+\cdots+c_1X_1+c_0$ with $c_0\in R^\times$, the relation gives$X_1^{-1}=-c_0^{-1}(X_1^{r-1}+c_{r-1}X_1^{r-2}+\cdots+c_2X_1+c_1).$ Also $T_i^{-1}=Q^{-1}(T_i-(Q-1))$, and each $X_j$ is a word in $X_1,T_1,\ldots,T_{j-1}$ by the affine recursion. Therefore closure under right multiplication by $X_1$ and the $T_i$ implies closure under all algebra generators and their inverses.

For each $\lambda$, the preceding steps and [F4] show that $N^{\unrhd\lambda}$ is a right ideal; applying $*$ gives a left ideal. Since $N^{\triangleright\lambda}$ is the sum of $N^{\unrhd\mu}$ over the finitely many minimal shapes $\mu\triangleright\lambda$, it too is a two-sided ideal. This proves the stated component-shift route.

Let $R_A=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1}]$ and let $H_n$ be the type-A Hecke algebra on $T_1,\ldots,T_{n-1}$ with braid relations and $(T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0$. For a partition $\lambda\vdash n$, let $t^\lambda$ be row-filled, $S_\lambda$ its row subgroup, $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and

Its inverse scans $i=n,n-1,\ldots,1$: find the unique component whose recording tableau contains $i$, delete that recording corner, and reverse-row-delete the corresponding box of its insertion tableau to recover $\sigma(i)$; the component is $\kappa_i$. $$ (T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\ (|i-j|>1), $$

$$ X_jX_k=X_kX_j,\qquad T_iX_j=X_jT_i\ (j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad T_iX_iT_i=QX_{i+1}. $$

Here the braid relation is imposed for $1\le i<n-1$ and the distant commutation relation for $1\le i,j<n$. Define the **multiplicative cyclotomic Hecke algebra of level $r$ and rank $n$** by

$$ H_{r,n}=\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{aff}}/(p(X_1)), $$

where $(p(X_1))$ denotes the two-sided ideal it generates. The unit $Q$ and the quadratic relation make every $T_i$ invertible, with $T_i^{-1}=Q^{-1}(T_i-(Q-1))$. The cyclotomic relation also gives the polynomial inverse

$$ X_1^{-1}=(-1)^{r+1}(u_1\cdots u_r)^{-1}\bigl(X_1^{r-1}-e_1X_1^{r-2}+\cdots+(-1)^{r-1}e_{r-1}\bigr), $$

where $e_k$ is the $k$th elementary symmetric polynomial in $u_1,\ldots,u_r$. The presentation already includes inverse generators; this formula records that the quotient does not require a separate inverse parameter. For $i\ge1$, write $X_{i+1}=Q^{-1}T_iX_iT_i$ when using the recursion determined by the affine relation.

This is the multiplicative presentation. It is not the additive degenerate cyclotomic presentation obtained after setting a parameter equal to $1$ and changing generators.

For an $r$-multipartition $\lambda$, put $a_c=\sum_{d<c}|\lambda^{(d)}|$ and define
$$u_\lambda=\prod_{c=2}^{r}\ \prod_{i=1}^{a_c}(L_i-u_c).$$
Let $t^\lambda$ be the row-standard initial multitableau from [[def-hh-cell-datum-dominance-and-cell-ideals]]. Let $S_\lambda$ be the subgroup of $S_n$ that permutes labels within each row of $t^\lambda$, and set $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$ and $m_\lambda=u_\lambda x_\lambda$. The anti-involution $*$ is the generator-fixing map of [[lem-hh-cyclotomic-anti-involution-fixes-generators]].

For a standard multitableau $t$, use the right entry action $t\cdot w:=w^{-1}\cdot t$, where the left action applies $w$ to every entry. Let $d(t)$ be the unique permutation with $t^\lambda\cdot d(t)=t$. Standardness implies that $d(t)$ is the distinguished minimal representative for its row-stabilizer coset. For standard $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$, define
$$m_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}.$$
These are specified elements of $H_{r,n}$; this definition does not assert their linear independence or cellularity.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $A$ be a unital associative $R$-algebra. A **cell datum** for $A$ consists of a finite poset $(\Lambda,\ge)$, finite sets $T(\lambda)$ for $\lambda\in\Lambda$, an $R$-basis $\{C^\lambda_{s,t}:\lambda\in\Lambda,\ s,t\in T(\lambda)\}$ of $A$, and an $R$-linear involutive algebra anti-automorphism $*$ satisfying $({C^\lambda_{s,t}})^*=C^\lambda_{t,s}$ and the following coefficient-independence axiom: for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$, $s,t\in T(\lambda)$, and $a\in A$, there are coefficients $r^\lambda_{t,v}(a)\in R$, independent of $s$, such that
$$C^\lambda_{s,t}a\equiv\sum_{v\in T(\lambda)}r^\lambda_{t,v}(a)C^\lambda_{s,v}\pmod{A^{>\lambda}},$$
where $A^{>\lambda}$ is the $R$-span of basis elements $C^\mu_{u,v}$ with $\mu>\lambda$. Write $A^{\ge\lambda}$ for the span with $\mu\ge\lambda$.

For multipartitions $\lambda,\mu$ of $n$ with $r$ ordered components, write $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ if for every component $1\le c\le r$ and row cutoff $j\ge0$,
$$\sum_{d<c}|\lambda^{(d)}|+\sum_{i=1}^{j}\lambda_i^{(c)} \ \ge\ \sum_{d<c}|\mu^{(d)}|+\sum_{i=1}^{j}\mu_i^{(c)},$$
with missing rows padded by zero. Write $\lambda\triangleright\mu$ when $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ and $\lambda\ne\mu$. The **row-standard initial multitableau** $t^\lambda$ fills component $1$ row by row, then component $2$ row by row, and so on, using $1,\ldots,n$ in order.

For each $\lambda\in\Lambda$, let $\Delta(\lambda)$ be the free $R$-module on symbols $c_t$ ($t\in T(\lambda)$), with right action
$$c_ta=\sum_{v\in T(\lambda)}r^\lambda_{t,v}(a)c_v.$$
Then this is a well-defined unital right $A$-module. In particular, after the cyclotomic Murphy basis theorem [[thm-hh-cyclotomic-murphy-basis-and-cellularity]], this construction gives its cell modules. There is a unique bilinear form $\langle\ ,\ \rangle_\lambda$ satisfying
$$C^\lambda_{s,t}C^\lambda_{u,v}\equiv\langle c_t,c_u\rangle_\lambda C^\lambda_{s,v}\pmod{A^{>\lambda}}.$$
The form is symmetric and satisfies $\langle xa,y\rangle_\lambda=\langle x,ya^*\rangle_\lambda$. Its radical is a right submodule, so the quotient by the radical is defined over $R$.

derivations.claim: For $(1,\varnothing)$ the cyclotomic factor is $X-b$ and the row subgroup is trivial; for $(\varnothing,1)$ the factor is empty and the row subgroup is trivial. Thus [F2] gives the displayed Murphy elements. In multipartition dominance the first component prefix is $1$ for $(1,\varnothing)$ and $0$ for $(\varnothing,1)$, so the stated order holds.

Expanding the relation gives $X^2=(a+b)X-ab$, hence $X^{-1}=(a+b-X)/(ab)$. Therefore the Laurent quotient equals the polynomial quotient $F[X]/((X-a)(X-b))$. Division by this monic quadratic gives a unique remainder of degree less than $2$, so $1,X$ is a basis. Since $X=m_1+b m_2$, the change from $1,X$ to $m_1,m_2$ has determinant $-1$; these Murphy elements are also a basis.

Direct multiplication gives$(X-b)X=X^2-bX=a(X-b).$ Thus for any $h=A(X-b)+B$ in the basis of step 2.1, $(X-b)h=(A(a-b)+B)(X-b)$, which is the fixed-row law in the upper cell. In the lower cell quotient, $X=(X-b)+b\equiv b$ modulo the upper ideal, so $1\cdot h\equiv h(b)\cdot1$. The involution fixes $X$ and hence both Murphy elements. These two calculations verify the cell axiom for both labels, so the displayed basis is cellular.
The upper form scalar is the coefficient in$(X-b)^2=(a-b)(X-b),$ so it is $a-b$. The lower basis element satisfies $1\cdot1=1$, giving form scalar $1$.

If $a=b=c\ne0$, then the defining polynomial is $(X-c)^2$. Translation by $c$ identifies the quotient with $F[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$, where $\epsilon=X-c$ is nonzero by the basis of step 2.1. The upper cell form is zero and the lower form is $1$. To see directly that there is one simple module, let $S$ be simple. The subspace $\epsilon S$ is a submodule. If it is nonzero then $\epsilon S=S$, which implies $\epsilon^2S=S$, contradicting $\epsilon^2=0$ and $S\ne0$. Thus $\epsilon S=0$, and $S$ is a simple module over $H/(\epsilon)\cong F$, hence one-dimensional.

Fix integers $r,n\ge1$. Put $R=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1},u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_r^{\pm1}]$ and $p(X)=\prod_{a=1}^r(X-u_a)$. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{aff}}$ be the unital associative $R$-algebra on generators $T_1,\ldots,T_{n-1}$ and $X_1^{\pm1},\ldots,X_n^{\pm1}$, with central $R$-action, subject to

$$ (T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\ (|i-j|>1), $$

$$ X_jX_k=X_kX_j,\qquad T_iX_j=X_jT_i\ (j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad T_iX_iT_i=QX_{i+1}. $$

Here the braid relation is imposed for $1\le i<n-1$ and the distant commutation relation for $1\le i,j<n$. Define the **multiplicative cyclotomic Hecke algebra of level $r$ and rank $n$** by

$$ H_{r,n}=\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{aff}}/(p(X_1)), $$

where $(p(X_1))$ denotes the two-sided ideal it generates. The unit $Q$ and the quadratic relation make every $T_i$ invertible, with $T_i^{-1}=Q^{-1}(T_i-(Q-1))$. The cyclotomic relation also gives the polynomial inverse

$$ X_1^{-1}=(-1)^{r+1}(u_1\cdots u_r)^{-1}\bigl(X_1^{r-1}-e_1X_1^{r-2}+\cdots+(-1)^{r-1}e_{r-1}\bigr), $$

where $e_k$ is the $k$th elementary symmetric polynomial in $u_1,\ldots,u_r$. The presentation already includes inverse generators; this formula records that the quotient does not require a separate inverse parameter. For $i\ge1$, write $X_{i+1}=Q^{-1}T_iX_iT_i$ when using the recursion determined by the affine relation.

This is the multiplicative presentation. It is not the additive degenerate cyclotomic presentation obtained after setting a parameter equal to $1$ and changing generators.

For standard $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$, define
$$m_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}.$$
These are specified elements of $H_{r,n}$; this definition does not assert their linear independence or cellularity.

$$c_ta=\sum_{v\in T(\lambda)}r^\lambda_{t,v}(a)c_v.$$
Then this is a well-defined unital right $A$-module. In particular, after the cyclotomic Murphy basis theorem [[thm-hh-cyclotomic-murphy-basis-and-cellularity]], this construction gives its cell modules. There is a unique bilinear form $\langle\ ,\ \rangle_\lambda$ satisfying

The form is symmetric and satisfies $\langle xa,y\rangle_\lambda=\langle x,ya^*\rangle_\lambda$. Its radical is a right submodule, so the quotient by the radical is defined over $R$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^\times$ and $\lambda\vdash n$, and write $\mu=\lambda'$, $L=\ell(w_\lambda)$ and $N=\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))$. Let $P(\lambda)=z_\lambda H$ with its DJ form $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$, the cell module $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ with its Murphy form $G_{\lambda'}$, and the sign automorphism $\theta$ be as in [[def-dj-bridge-row-column-permutation-modules-and-polytabloids]], [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]], and let $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta$ be the $\theta$-twisted cell module of [[lem-dj-bridge-theta-transport-of-the-cellular-structure]]. Then:

1. There is a base-change compatible isomorphism of right $H$-modules $$\Phi_\lambda\colon P(\lambda)\longrightarrow C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta,\qquad \Phi_\lambda(z_\lambda)=m_0,\quad \Phi_\lambda(z_\lambda h)=m_0\theta(h)\ \ (h\in H),$$ where $m_0$ is the class of $x_{\lambda'}$ in $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and the right side is computed with the ordinary action on $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and read in the twist; in particular $\Phi_\lambda(e_t)=m_0\theta(T_{d_{\lambda'}(t)})$ for $t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda')$. For a class $m\in C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and any lift $\widetilde m\in M(\lambda')$, the inverse is $\Phi_\lambda^{-1}(m)=q^{-N}x_\lambda T_{w_\lambda}\theta(\widetilde m)$, independently of the chosen lift.

2. With $G_{\lambda'}^\theta$ the transported form of [[lem-dj-bridge-theta-transport-of-the-cellular-structure]] and $u_\lambda(q):=q^{\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))-\ell(w_\lambda)}\in A^\times$, $$G_{\lambda'}^\theta(\Phi_\lambda x,\Phi_\lambda y)=u_\lambda(q)\,\beta_{P(\lambda)}(x,y)\qquad(x,y\in P(\lambda)),$$ over every commutative $R$ with $q\in R^\times$. No unnamed scalar and no potentially vanishing scalar occurs: $u_\lambda$ is the explicit unit $q^{N-L}$ in the fixed normalizations of this page.

3. Consequently $\Phi_\lambda$ maps the radical of $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ onto the radical of $G_{\lambda'}^\theta$, the induced map between the quotients is an isomorphism, with the corresponding cell-form quotients $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}\cong(D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^\theta$, including the zero-quotient case. Over a field, when the quotients are nonzero they are the simple heads; when the forms are identically zero, the displayed quotients are zero and no assertion about the actual module heads is made. Over a PID with a chosen prime, the unit-scaled form identity preserves all divisibility submodules and their reductions. One also obtains $P(\lambda')\cong P(\lambda)^{\circ,\theta}$ with the exact position of the dual and the twist, separating same-shape duality from conjugate-sign transport. No choice principle is used.

derivations.claim: The quadratic relation is $T^2=(Q-1)T+Q$. The row subgroup of $(2)$ is $S_2$, giving row sum $1+T$; the row subgroup of $(1,1)$ is trivial, giving $1$. The partition dominance inequalities give $(2)\triangleright(1,1)$.

Monic division by $(T-Q)(T+1)$ gives basis $1,T$ for $H$. Since $T=(1+T)-1$, the pair $1+T,1$ is also a basis. Direct multiplication gives$(1+T)^2=1+2T+T^2=(Q+1)(1+T).$ Also $T(1+T)=Q(1+T)$, while $T=(1+T)-1\equiv-1$ modulo the upper cell. Thus each cell has the required fixed-row action, and the involution fixes both basis elements; this verifies the cellular basis directly.

By [F4] the upper cell form is the coefficient $Q+1$ in the displayed square, and the lower cell form is $1\cdot1=1$. At $Q=-1$, $(T+1)^2=0$ and $T+1$ is nonzero because it is a basis element. The upper form vanishes and the lower form remains $1$. The algebra is $F[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with $\epsilon=T+1$. For any simple right module $S$, $\epsilon S$ is a submodule; if it were nonzero then $\epsilon S=S$, forcing $\epsilon^2S=S$, contrary to $\epsilon^2=0$. Hence $\epsilon S=0$, and $S$ is the unique one-dimensional module with $T=-1$.

The cross-link in [F5] places the ordinary Specht module at the conjugate Murphy label and applies the sign twist. The calculation above concerns the row-Murphy labels $(2)$ and $(1,1)$, so the comparison requires both operations and does not identify the row cell at $\lambda$ with an untwisted Specht module at $\lambda$.

Let $R_A=\mathbb Z[Q^{\pm1}]$ and let $H_n$ be the type-A Hecke algebra on $T_1,\ldots,T_{n-1}$ with braid relations and $(T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0$. For a partition $\lambda\vdash n$, let $t^\lambda$ be row-filled, $S_\lambda$ its row subgroup, $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and
$$m_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*x_\lambda T_{d(t)}$$
for standard $\lambda$-tableaux, with the tableau action and distinguished representatives fixed in [[def-hh-cyclotomic-murphy-elements]]. Then the $m_{st}$ form an $R_A$-basis of $H_n$, $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$, and the spans $H_n^{\trianglerighteq\lambda}$ and $H_n^{\triangleright\lambda}$ of shapes respectively dominating and strictly dominating $\lambda$ are two-sided ideals. For every $h\in H_n$ and standard $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$,
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}r_{t,v}(h)m_{sv}\pmod{H_n^{\triangleright\lambda}},$$
where $r_{t,v}(h)\in R_A$ does not depend on $s$. The proof is integral over $R_A$; it does not divide by $Q+1$ or assume semisimplicity.

Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^{\times}$, let $e=e(F,q)$ and assume $e>n$ (with $e=\infty$ allowed); let $\lambda\vdash n$, $H=H_{F,q}(S_n)$, and let $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ be the Murphy cell module with Murphy basis $(m_t)_{t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]).

1. (**Separation**) If $s,t$ are standard $\lambda$-tableaux with $[\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q$ for all $1\le k\le n$ then $s=t$. More precisely, if the q-content values agree for all $k\notin\{i,i+1\}$ for some $i$, then $s=t$ or $t=s(i\ i+1)$. 2. (**Idempotents**) Let $\mathcal R_k$ be the set of distinct q-content values of the entry $k$ over standard tableaux of **all** partitions of $n$. For a standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ define $$F_t:=\prod_{k=1}^{n}\ \prod_{\substack{c\in\mathcal R_k\\        c\ne[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q}}        \frac{L_k-c}{[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q-c}\in F[L_1,\ldots,L_n].$$ These are orthogonal idempotents of $H$; their actions on $S_{\mathrm M}^\lambda$ project onto the corresponding simultaneous eigenlines. Put $f_t=m_tF_t$. Then $f_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_qf_t$ and $f_t=m_t+\sum_{s\rhd t}a_sm_s$. The global content sets are essential for the asserted idempotency in $H$, rather than only the induced same-shape endomorphisms. 3. (**Orthogonal seminormal basis**) $\{f_t:t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)\}$ is a basis of $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ satisfying $f_tF_s=\delta_{ts}f_t$ and $\langle f_s,f_t\rangle_\lambda=\delta_{st}\langle f_t,f_t\rangle_\lambda$; it is the **seminormal basis** of the Murphy cell module. 4. (**Generator action**) Let $s$ be a standard $\lambda$-tableau, $1\le i<n$ and $t:=s(i\ i+1)$, and put $\rho:=\operatorname{content}_s(i)-\operatorname{content}_s(i+1)\in\mathbb Z$. If $i$ and $i+1$ lie in the same row of $s$ then $f_sT_i=q\,f_s$; if they lie in the same column then $f_sT_i=-f_s$; otherwise $t$ is standard and $$f_sT_i=\alpha_i(s)\,f_t-\frac{1}{[\rho]_q}f_s,\qquad \alpha_i(s):=\begin{cases}1,&s\rhd t,\\[1mm]\dfrac{[1+\rho]_q[1-\rho]_q}{[\rho]_q[-\rho]_q},&t\rhd s,\end{cases}$$ where $[-\rho]_q$ is the extended quantum integer of [[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]] and for the swapped tableau $\operatorname{content}_t(i)-\operatorname{content}_t(i+1)=-\rho$. No semisimplicity of $H$ is assumed and no choice principle is used.

Fix $r,n\ge1$ and work in the universal cyclotomic algebra $H_{r,n}$ of [[def-hh-multiplicative-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]], with parameters $Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r$, commuting Jucys–Murphy generators $L_i=X_i$, and finite generators $T_i$. For an $r$-multipartition $\lambda$, put $a_c=\sum_{d<c}|\lambda^{(d)}|$ and define
$$u_\lambda=\prod_{c=2}^{r}\ \prod_{i=1}^{a_c}(L_i-u_c).$$
Let $t^\lambda$ be the row-standard initial multitableau from [[def-hh-cell-datum-dominance-and-cell-ideals]]. Let $S_\lambda$ be the subgroup of $S_n$ that permutes labels within each row of $t^\lambda$, and set $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$ and $m_\lambda=u_\lambda x_\lambda$. The anti-involution $*$ is the generator-fixing map of [[lem-hh-cyclotomic-anti-involution-fixes-generators]].

For a standard multitableau $t$, use the right entry action $t\cdot w:=w^{-1}\cdot t$, where the left action applies $w$ to every entry. Let $d(t)$ be the unique permutation with $t^\lambda\cdot d(t)=t$. Standardness implies that $d(t)$ is the distinguished minimal representative for its row-stabilizer coset. For standard $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$, define
$$m_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}.$$
These are specified elements of $H_{r,n}$; this definition does not assert their linear independence or cellularity.

Fix $r,n\ge1$ and use the independent units $Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r$ of [[def-hh-multiplicative-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]. An **$r$-multipartition** of $n$ is a tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(r)})$ of ordinary partitions whose total number of boxes is $n$. Its boxes are triples $(c,a,b)$ with $1\le c\le r$, $a\ge1$, and $1\le b\le\lambda^{(c)}_a$. Order the boxes within component $c$ by the transitive closure of $(c,a,b)<(c,a,b+1)$ and $(c,a,b)<(c,a+1,b)$; boxes in different components are incomparable.

A **standard multitableau** $t$ of shape $\lambda$ is a bijective filling of the boxes by $1,\ldots,n$ that increases along every row and column. Equivalently, it is a linear extension of this finite box poset. Write $\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)$ for the set of such fillings and

$$ \operatorname{res}_t(i)=u_cQ^{b-a}\quad\text{if entry }i\text{ occupies }(c,a,b). $$

The **generic content field** is $K=\mathbb Q(Q,u_1,\ldots,u_r)$, the fraction field of $R$. The contents of distinct addable boxes of any multipartition are distinct in $K$. If two boxes in one component have the same content, they lie on one diagonal; the right and lower boxes immediately between them are distinct required predecessors of the southeast box. Consequently, for three consecutive labels $i,i+1,i+2$ in a standard multitableau, the first and third contents cannot agree. In particular every pair of contents among three consecutive labels is distinct in $K$. If two boxes in one component have content exponents differing by $1$, then they are comparable in the box order, so interchanging adjacent labels in a standard multitableau never gives a content ratio $Q$ or $Q^{-1}$.

derivations.claim: Work first over $K$. For standard $u,v$ of shape $\mu$, define the endomorphism $R_{uv}$ by $wR_{uv}=\langle w,f_u\rangle f_v$ on $W_\mu$, and by zero on other $W_\nu$. Nonsingularity makes these a basis of $\bigoplus_\mu\operatorname{End}_K(W_\mu)$. The faithful action map of [F2] is a $K$-linear isomorphism onto this endomorphism space because its dimensions agree. Thus the $R_{uv}$ are coordinates for $H_{n,K}$. Invariance gives $w(T_iR_{uv})=\langle w,f_uT_i\rangle f_v$ and $w(R_{uv}T_i)=\langle w,f_u\rangle(f_vT_i)$. Left multiplication therefore changes only $u$, right multiplication only $v$, and each changes its index only to itself or its standard adjacent swap; both directions of a standard swap have nonzero coefficients.

We need a comparison valid across shapes. Let $b$ be row standard with $i$ in an upper row and $i+1$ in a lower row, and put $b'=b(i,i+1)$. If standard $a\unrhd_{\rm tab}b$, then $a\unrhd_{\rm tab}b'$ and every standard swap $a'=a(i,i+1)$ also dominates $b'$. Only the cutoff $m=i$ changes. A swap raising $a$'s counts causes no problem. For a lowering swap, a failure at row cutoff $j$ would require $A_a(j,i)=A_b(j,i)$ while $b$'s swap does not lower its count at $j$. If both labels lie above $j$ in $b$, then $A_a(j,i+1)=A_b(j,i)<A_b(j,i+1)$, contradicting $a\unrhd_{\rm tab}b$. If both lie below $j$, then $A_a(j,i-1)=A_b(j,i)-1<A_b(j,i-1)$, again a contradiction. These exhaust the possible failures.

Let $B_r$ be the interval of labels occupying row $r$ of $t^\alpha$, and write $x_\alpha=\sum a_{uv}R_{uv}$. Fix a right index $v$ and an adjacent pair $i,i+1$ inside $B_r$. Comparing coefficients in $T_ix_\alpha=Qx_\alpha$, if $i,i+1$ share a column of $u$, gives $-a_{uv}=Qa_{uv}$; no other first index can contribute because $u(i,i+1)$ is not standard. Hence $a_{uv}=0$. If $u'=u(i,i+1)$ is standard, its coefficient equation has the form $Qa_{uv}=c_ua_{uv}+a_{u'}a_{u'v}$, where $a_{u'}\ne0$ is the seminormal off-diagonal scalar. Thus $a_{uv}=0$ forces $a_{u'v}=0$, and the reverse implication follows from the equation at $u'$. Zeros therefore propagate across every standard swap inside a block $B_r$.

Any two linear extensions of a finite poset are connected by adjacent incomparable swaps: move the first desired element left across its predecessors in the other extension, all of which must be incomparable, and continue inductively.
